published_inputs.author: J. S. Milne
published_inputs.title: Abelian Varieties
published_inputs.edition: Corrected 2022 version of the 1986 Storrs article
published_inputs.field_scope: Arbitrary base fields, including positive characteristic; used here over the original algebraically closed K.
published_inputs.attribution: Published input retained explicitly; not newly proved and not attributed to a post-proof exposition.
published_inputs.exact_used_statement: An ample invertible sheaf with a nonzero section on an abelian variety has a translation stabilizer of dimension zero.

published_inputs.title: Abelian Varieties
published_inputs.edition: Corrected 2022 version of the 1986 Storrs article
published_inputs.field_scope: Arbitrary base fields, including positive characteristic; used here over the original algebraically closed K.
published_inputs.attribution: Published input retained explicitly; not newly proved and not attributed to a post-proof exposition.
published_inputs.exact_used_statement: If the translation stabilizer has dimension zero, the invertible sheaf has nonzero cohomology in exactly one degree.

published_inputs.exact_used_statement: For a Cartier divisor D on an abelian variety of dimension g, chi(O(D))=(D^g)/g!, as an equality in Q of integer-valued numerical invariants.

background_references.scope_note: Smoothness over a field gives regular local rings; regular local rings are domains; smooth relative dimension equals fiber dimension. Also the ordinary sheaf gluing, affine closed-immersion criterion, Veronese embedding and Zariski lemma.
